source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Offer scheduled toileting assistance to reduce urgency-related unassisted bathroom trips","B":"Restrict the client's fluid intake substantially to prevent every nighttime bathroom trip","C":"Use scheduled toileting as the only fall-prevention intervention needed for the client","D":"Avoid toileting schedules because elimination needs have no relationship to fall risk"}}
source_row.rationale: A scheduled toileting program proactively addresses a client's elimination needs at regular intervals, which can help reduce the fall risk associated with urgency and unassisted nighttime bathroom trips — an evidence-based component of a comprehensive, individualized fall prevention plan, used alongside other appropriate interventions.
source_row.source_detail: Scheduled rounding protocol includes toileting assistance as a tailored fall-prevention intervention; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: AHRQ — Preventing Falls in Hospitals / Scheduled Rounding
source_row.stem: A nurse implements a scheduled toileting program for a client at high risk for falls related to urgency and nighttime bathroom trips, and a family member wonders whether this alone is really expected to make a meaningful difference. This intervention is intended to:
